subject: Per-account routing guarantee & compliance gating for Odyssey Bank (OD-5732)

Subject: Per-account routing guarantee & compliance gating for Odyssey Bank (OD-5732)

Team —

Quick ask from the field: Odyssey (large regional bank, deal OD-5732) has signaled they will only move to signature if we provide a firm per-account routing guarantee and an auditable activation policy for a subset of endpoints (redaction + tenant affinity). High level: they need a "routing guarantee" that ensures requests from their tenant are pinned to a deterministic serving path (model variant + region + residency when possible) and that we can produce a short audit proving those routes were used for a given time window.

Why this matters: procurement has regulatory reviewers who require reproducible routing for certain regulated workflows (KYC, AML checks). Without it they will either require higher contractual indemnities or walk. This is a $1.2M ARR new account ramp.

Acceptance criteria we heard from them:
- Tenant-level routing pinning for chosen model variants (can be a configuration flag per-tenant)
- Exportable audit CSV for routing decisions (time, model-id, node-id, route-policy) for a 30-day lookback
- Graceful fallback policy (if pin unavailable, fallback to approved compatible model variant + an alert)
- Documentation and a short attestation we can share with their compliance team

Asks from product/eng: can you provide a surface-level feasibility note and an initial T-shirt estimate (spike + implementation) so I can push this into the commercial negotiation this week?

Attachments: odyssey_security_summary.pdf (summary of their compliance ask)

Timeline: Odyssey wants a statement by EOD Friday 2026-11-05; procurement deadline 2026-11-12.

Thanks — I know this is tight.
Mina

Subject: Re: Per-account routing guarantee & compliance gating for Odyssey Bank (OD-5732)

Thanks Mina — good summary. Quick clarifying questions before I pull in product ops and schedule a spike:

1) Is the requirement that routing be deterministically repeatable for the same input (i.e., identical requests always route the same way), or simply that we can produce a record of the routing decisions that occurred (auditability)?
2) How many model variants would Odyssey expect to lock to? (one primary + one fallback? multiple?)
3) Traffic profile: what peak QPS and token-per-request should we design for the initial phase?

Initial thoughts: we may be able to treat this as a configurable routing policy (tenant tag + affinity key) and wire audit events from the router into an exportable CSV. The trick will be guaranteeing determinism across failovers and autoscaling; that will likely push to a node-affinity + consistent-hash approach or persistent affinity cookie that we can honor in the router.

If you can answer the three bullets above I can ask Eng to estimate spike vs. full work. If it's primarily "auditability" with a reasonable fallback window, the implementation complexity drops.

–Marissa
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Per-account routing guarantee & compliance gating for Odyssey Bank (OD-5732)

Marissa — answers inline and added Felix + Maggie for visibility.

> 1) Deterministically repeatable or just auditable?
Felix: their compliance team prefers deterministic repeatability for flagged flows (they call them "verifiable pipelines"), but they said an auditable approach with short windows (e.g., daily CSV exports) might be acceptable as an interim contractual commitment while we build full determinism.

> 2) How many model variants?
They want one primary model (v1) pinned and one approved fallback variant.

> 3) Traffic profile?
Expectations for pilot (months 0–3):
- Peak: 55 rps (reads) for verification flows
- Average tokens per request: 400
- Production ramp target (months 3–12): steady 150 rps

Felix / Maggie — procurement deadline: 2026-11-12 (need a signed SOW). If product/eng can give a conservative estimate (spike + 2 options: fast-track minimal, full solution) I will include that in our commercial redlines.

Attaching odyssey_security_summary.pdf for internal QA.

Mina

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Per-account routing guarantee & compliance gating for Odyssey Bank (OD-5732)

Thanks for the details — feasible but non-trivial. High-level engineering assessment: 

Option A – Interim (fast-track, minimal risk):
- Implement tenant-level audit export: router writes routing decision events (timestamp, tenant-id, model-id, node-id, route-policy) to a durable topic and an export job generates daily CSVs.
- Build a per-tenant config flag to prefer a model-id; do not guarantee deterministic routing across scale events (documented limitation).
- Spike: 1 week to wire events + export pipeline. Implementation: 2 weeks.
- Risk: customers may still push for deterministic proof across failover windows.

Option B – Full guarantee (deterministic routing):
- Add persistent affinity keys + consistent-hash ring and node pinning for tenant-bound traffic, add replication of affinity state to survive node failures, and surface a verification endpoint that can re-run routing decisions for a past request for audit purposes.
- Spike: 3 weeks (design + POC). Implementation: 4–6 weeks.
- Risk: medium — requires infra-level changes and careful failure-mode testing.

Dependencies and notes:
- Need product to lock acceptance criteria for fallback behavior and SLAs during failover.
- Need security/legal to sign off on storage/retention of routing logs (PII considerations).

I'll draft a short RFC summarizing Option A vs B and estimated schedule. For planning: I can commit a spike for the week of 2026-11-08.

Attachment: routing_policy_rfc.md (draft plan)

—Rishi
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Great — thanks Rishi.

Plan of record (proposal to close commercial ask this week):
- Commit to Option A as an interim contractual deliverable (spike + 2 weeks implementation).
- Run a product/eng canary with Odyssey for 2 weeks to validate export CSVs and the per-tenant preference flag.
- Start Option B spike in parallel if legal/compliance requires deterministic guarantees; evaluate after canary.

Mina: I'll prepare a short one-page product note and a mitigation plan to share with Odyssey and their procurement team. Can you lock a quick call with Felix + Maggie Thursday 2026-11-05 10:00am ET? If we get their verbal buy-in on Option A + canary, procurement can accept a springboard clause for Option B.

Irene: please advise on whether security/legal need to be looped in now for the storage/retention ask.

If everyone is aligned I will add the spike to Eng planning and mark this as a candidate for next sprint.

–Marissa
